**6B.9 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed (2024)**

**Bottom line:** Mixed, leaning no. I found real 2024 institution-building in monetary governance, education, refugee access, displacement policy, and transitional justice, but most of it is still donor-backed, launch-stage, or official rhetoric rather than proof of durable institutions that would outlast Abiy personally. The strongest counterevidence is that emergency centralization, covert security structures, and repression of watchdogs remained active.

**Evidence**
- [The Council of Ministers today approved the draft NBE Proclamation and Banking Business Proclamation](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-council-of-ministers-today-approved-the-draft-nbe-proclamation-and-banking-business-proclamation/) - National Bank of Ethiopia, 2024-06-14. Claim: the draft laws were described as strengthening credibility, accountability, transparency, and governance in the central bank and banking sector, which is a real attempt to harden an economic institution. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.4, 6B.5.
- [The National Bank of Ethiopia announces the launch of a new monetary policy framework](https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-national-bank-of-ethiopia-announces-the-launch-of-a-new-monetary-policy-framework/) - National Bank of Ethiopia, 2024-07-09. Claim: NBE said it had enhanced technical capacity and moved to an interest-rate-based, price-stability framework, which looks like durable institution-building rather than ad hoc personal rule. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.4, 6B.5.
- [WHO Ethiopia country profile 2024](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/ethiopia) - World Health Organization, 2024. Claim: Ethiopia’s PHC framework was developed through a multisectoral process involving government, partners, academia, and the private sector, with emphasis on governance, workforce, and transparent procurement. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.4, 6B.5, 6B.6.
- [Building a strong foundation to improve learning outcomes in AFE Ethiopia](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia) - World Bank, 2024-09-05. Claim: GEQIP-E trained over 102,000 teachers, improved girls’ enrollment in disadvantaged regions, and supported refugee schools, which is a concrete social-institution investment. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.8, 6B.4, 6B.6.
- [Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services](https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services) - UNHCR Africa, 2024-03-07. Claim: the refugee ID rollout was designed to let nearly one million refugees access basic national services, which is one of the clearest durable-inclusion signals in the record. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.8, 6B.6, 6B.7.
- [Ethiopia launches national strategy to implement solutions pathways in internal displacement](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/283776-ethiopia-launches-national-strategy-implement-solutions-pathways-internal-displacement) - UN Ethiopia / UNHCR, 2024-11-11. Claim: the government and UN launched a strategy for voluntary return, local integration, reintegration, coordination, and accountability for IDPs, which is a plausible institutional template beyond one-off relief. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.6, 6B.8.
- [UN Women supports Civil Society Organizations’ engagement in transitional justice policy](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/283986-un-women-supports-civil-society-organizations%E2%80%99-engagement-transitional-justice-policy) - United Nations in Ethiopia, 2024-09-09. Claim: women leaders and grassroots groups were brought into transitional-justice implementation with an explicit gender-sensitivity goal, which is positive for institutional legitimacy and durability. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.8.
- [The government said the transitional justice policy is meant to address accountability, truth-seeking, conditional amnesty, reconciliation, and institutional reform](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876) - ENA English, 2024-12-14. Claim: the state publicly framed transitional justice as an institutional reform project, but this is still roadmap rhetoric rather than proof that institutions had become self-sustaining. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.8, 6B.5.
- [The proclamation centralized coercive authority, allowed replacement of local administrators, restricted CSOs and media, and suspended normal judicial handling of enforcement](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124) - ENA English, 2024-11-03. Claim: the emergency design centralized power and narrowed institutional autonomy, which cuts against the idea of durable institutions independent of Abiy. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.5.
- [Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-03-04. Claim: HRW reported arbitrary arrests of opposition figures and journalists and an atmosphere where no one appeared safe from arbitrary detention, which is the opposite of institution-building that survives personal rule. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.5.
- [World Report 2024: Ethiopia](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-01-12. Claim: HRW described a coordinated food-aid diversion scheme and forced evictions, showing that core social institutions were still vulnerable to capture and coercion rather than durable neutrality. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.6.
- [Reuters via EHRC on secret committee](https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/) - Reuters via EHRC, 2024-02-27. Claim: the EHRC head said a secret security committee interfered in the justice system and was tied to widespread human-rights violations, which suggests parallel coercive governance rather than resilient public institutions. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.5.
- [Ethiopia: Authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/) - Amnesty International, 2024-02-19. Claim: emergency powers were used for warrantless arrests, movement limits, and bans on assemblies, which weakens any claim that durable rule-bound institutions were being built. IDs: 6B.9, also 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.5.

**Search gap**
- I found many reform launches, strategies, and capacity-building programs, but almost no direct evidence that these institutions were legally insulated from Abiy, financially independent, or likely to survive a turnover in power.
- The positive evidence is mostly donor-backed or official process evidence, so durability has to be inferred from design, not demonstrated by long-run performance.
